Kalman filter and smoother estimates from a julia backend fit

Source: R/ctBackendKalman.R
ctBackendKalman.Rd

Prior, filtered and smoothed estimates of the latent states and the observations, for every row of data, from the same forward pass the engine uses for the likelihood. ctKalmanArray (alias ctStanKalman) dispatches here for a ctJuliaFit, so call that unless you want the julia route specifically. ctPredict (alias ctKalman) returns the same information as a long data frame.

Usage

ctBackendKalman(
  fit,
  subjects = "all",
  timestep = "asdata",
  maxtime = "asdata",
  removeObs = FALSE,
  pointest = TRUE,
  nsamples = NA,
  collapsefunc = NA,
  standardisederrors = FALSE,
  subjectpars = FALSE,
  indvarstates = FALSE,
  randomEffects = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

A ctJuliaFit.

subjects

'all', a vector of subject ids, or integer positions into the fitted subjects.

timestep

'asdata' to use the observed times, 'auto' to choose an interpolation step, or a positive number.

maxtime

Only used when interpolating: the largest time to compute for.

removeObs

TRUE withholds every observation so that only expectations given parameters and covariates are returned; a positive integer N keeps every Nth.

pointest

Use the point estimate as the single sample.

nsamples

Number of posterior draws to use when pointest=FALSE.

collapsefunc

Function applied over draws, e.g. mean.

standardisederrors

Also return residuals standardised by the prior observation covariance.

subjectpars

Also return each subject's own model matrices.

indvarstates

Keep the augmented individual-difference states in the latent output rather than trimming to the real processes. On a single level of Laplace random effects, where the effects are not states, they are appended as if they were: predicted and updated from the subject's rows before and up to each row, smoothed from its whole record, on the raw scale as deviations from the population value. Their covariances with the latent states are not computed and are NA.

randomEffects

For an `intoverpop='laplace'` fit, which levels of random effect the trajectories are built from. Naming one of the model's id columns includes that level and every level outside it, so the innermost id gives each subject its own trajectory and an outer id gives the group mean, shared by every subject in the group. `'population'` includes none, giving the trajectory implied by the population parameters alone. Defaults to the innermost id. Ignored for other fits.

With one level of random effects, left in, the predicted and updated passes take each subject's effects at their posterior given its rows up to each row (`ctsem_laplace_sequential`), and the smoothed pass at their mode given its whole record. Otherwise every pass takes the whole-record modes. A message says which once per call.

The whole-record modes are the ones the fit arrived at, and they stay fixed however this call changes the rows being filtered. Selecting subjects, interpolating a time grid or withholding observations with removeObs therefore leaves them alone: with every observation withheld the smoothed pass still uses that subject's own random effects.

...

Passed to collapsefunc.

Value

A list of arrays, the same shape ctKalmanArray returns for Stan fits, with subjectMatrices attached when subjectpars=TRUE.

Details

Internal. ctBackend* means internal throughout the package, so this is not exported; users reach it through ctKalmanArray and ctPredict, which dispatch here for a ctJuliaFit. The randomEffects notes below describe behaviour those two inherit.

Individual-difference parameters come out of the smoothed initial state: ctsem carries an individually varying parameter as an augmented latent state with no drift and no diffusion, so its smoothed t0 estimate is the subject's value for it.

Examples

# \donttest{
# ctBackendKalman(fit, timestep = .1)
# }
